newsitem.title: GUATEMALA: Guatemala's new police trained to respect rights.
newsitem.headline: Guatemala's new police trained to respect rights.

text.p: Guatemalan police began an effort to shake a dark history of corruption, murder and brutality with the graduation of police officers on Tuesday from a new academy that teaches respect for human rights.
"The police is not an institution to repress. Above all it is an institution to serve citizens," Interior Minister Rodolfo Mendoza told the 1,200 new officers at the ceremony.

During 36 years of civil war, which ended last year with a historic peace signing, the Guatemalan police were widely accused of carrying out assassinations and torture at the behest of military regimes.

Under the terms of the peace accord, the government formed the National Civilian Police force and began to retrain members of the former police staff and attract new recruits. A special training group of Civil Guardsmen from Spain gave classes on human rights and modern police techniques.
The Military Police will be phased out and members of the National Guard will become part of the civilian police, as part of a larger effort to demilitarize Guatemalan society.
By 1999 the new academy was scheduled to turn out 20,000 new and retrained police officers. The current police force is less than 10,000 strong and the National Guard has 4,000 members.
